analysis:
Examined the new AdmissionRateEstimators.swift, the LaunchAgent.swift allowlist change, and the added tests (a87b032d25abc758:0 is a test file with metadata only; its patch excerpt was truncated, so its content was not fully reviewed).

The LaunchAgent change (lines 268-269, 285) only adds DARKBLOOM_TTFT_ADMISSION_FIXES to the inferencePassthroughEnvKeys allowlist. It forwards a non-empty value from the installing shell into the launchd plist, the same as the other tuning knobs. This is not a secret or an auth-relevant value, and the allowlist stays fixed and small, so it adds no new injection surface.

The new estimators (AdmissionRateEstimators.swift) affect only local TTFT deadline admission, which is an availability and performance control. IsolatedPrefillAdmissionRate.resolve filters non-finite and non-positive inputs. It floors admission pricing at 1/8 of the idle calibration anchor, and it drops idle evidence older than 30 minutes. DeadlineAdmissionFixes.decodeRateShape keeps the per-row charge for calibrated policies, preserving the reviewed error-envelope assumption. The kill switch is parsed on exact off values and defaults to on.

No change touches the encrypted prefix-cache storage, key handling, attestation, App Attest authorization, WebSocket protocol, or plaintext handling (T-041, T-008, TB-011, TB-002), so none of those threat-model assumptions are affected.

A residual availability and fairness question remains. The anchor-based recovery could slightly admit more work while the GPU is contended by another process; the file's comments acknowledge this. This is a performance policy issue, not a confidentiality or integrity issue. It is worth a later review of the callers in EngineV2Bridge, which were not supplied, including how the `admissionFixes` parameter and the calibrated-policy gating are wired. That integration is outside the supplied evidence, so I record it as an unverified contract rather than a finding.
